title: Dual-mode embeddings ingestion: streaming edge-forwarder + atomic batch commit
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem statement: customers need both low-latency incremental ingestion for near-real-time search/reranking and high-throughput bulk imports for initial dataset loads. Current endpoints either support synchronous small batches or large async jobs with brittle retry semantics. This ticket proposes a dual-mode ingestion API: a streaming-forwarder for sub-second ingestion and an atomic commit async batch API with first-class idempotency and deterministic partial-commit semantics.

API surface (summary):
- POST /v1/embeddings/stream (streaming-forwarder): client sends NDJSON or protobuf frames; server ACKs per-blob with short-lived commit lease token. Best-effort low-latency indexing + KV-cache write.
- POST /v1/embeddings/batches (create batch job): client uploads manifest or multipart payload and receives batch_job_id + idempotency_key echo.
- POST /v1/embeddings/batches/{batch_job_id}/commit: attempts atomic apply of prepared records. If interrupted, commit is idempotent and safe to retry.
- GET /v1/embeddings/batches/{batch_job_id}/status: job-level progress, per-shard success/failure counts, repo-style commit hash for deterministic snapshot.

Idempotency semantics: idempotency_key is opaque string provided by client (max 256 bytes). Server persists idempotency_key -> final commit result mapping for 7 days. For streaming-forwarder we use per-event client-provided dedupe_id plus an epoch and server-assigned lease token; replays within lease are deduplicated, replays after lease may be reingested but marked as replay in audit logs.

Partial failure model: batch upload and prepare phase can succeed while commit fails. The system records a prepare checkpoint and exposes a resume token. Commits are executed as a two-phase apply against the embeddings store to maintain atomicity per-batch_job_id. For very large batches we chunk commit into ordered shards but publish a top-level commit when all shards confirm. If a shard fails, automatic rollback of previously applied shards occurs, or the job is moved to FAILED with an explicit remediation plan.

Sharding and scaling: batches are sharded by customer_id + consistent hash on dedupe_id to allow parallel preparation and reduce cross-partition coordination during commit. Streaming-forwarder routes small writes to hot GPU indexing nodes for immediate availability (low-latency reads), while batches are routed to cold indexing lanes with higher throughput and background quant/normalize tasks.

Observability and SLOs: add metrics for per-job latency, prepare-duration, commit-duration, idempotent-hit-rate, dedupe-rate, and reingest_count. Add tracing spans for prepare->commit and a new dashboards/alerts in Console under "Embeddings Ingest".

Compatibility with reranking: store normalized vectors and keep a lightweight metadata shard that can be queried for reranker feature extraction without full index warm-up. Batch commits surface a materialization checkpoint that downstream rerankers can watch and fetch incremental delta vectors.

Security and quotas: enforce per-customer concurrent batch_job limits, rate-limit streaming-forwarder by token, and validate idempotency keys for length/charset. All temporary prepare blobs are encrypted at rest and retention limited to 7 days by default.

Why this is different: existing uploads focus on single-mode designs (continuous ndjson or multipart). This approach treats ingestion as a first-class choreography (prepare/commit), providing deterministic, idempotent commits and a low-latency stream path without compromising large-scale throughput or recovery semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming-forwarder accepts NDJSON frames and returns per-frame ACK with lease token
Batch API supports create/prepare/commit/status lifecycle and persists idempotency_key mapping for 7 days
System deduplicates replays within lease window for streaming-forwarder and returns replay audit flag when outside lease
Batch commits are atomic at the job level: either visible as full commit or marked FAILED with rollback applied
End-to-end integration test covering upload -> prepare shard -> commit -> reranker materialization passes in CI
Console dashboard shows batch_job success/failure rates and per-customer concurrency metrics
design_decisions: Idempotency key is opaque to server; server stores SHA256(idempotency_key) to avoid leaking client tokens
Lease TTL for streaming ACKs default 5 minutes; configurable per-customer up to 1 hour
Commit uses a 2-phase apply with per-shard tombstones to allow safe rollback
Per-customer partitioning to limit blast radius and enable independent replays/backfills
Prepare artifacts encrypted and retained for 7 days to allow late commits without permanent storage bloat
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable streaming-forwarder for 5 internal customers; monitor dedupe-hit-rate and commit latencies
Phase 2: open batch create/prepare for public beta with 24/7 monitoring and fast rollback playbook
Phase 3: GA with CLI/SDK additions and migration tool for existing large uploads
Fallback policy: if commit consistently fails for a tenant, auto-disable commit and surface an actionable incident with remediation steps
migrations: Backfill: compute per-customer materialization checkpoint for existing indices to make batch commits compatible with reranker delta pulls
Index update: add normalized_vector column and batch_commit_id metadata to embeddings table
Retention policy: schedule GC job to remove prepare artifacts older than 7 days
